pages.title: Output Port
pages.text: Output ports mark an active extraction point. If a usable output port exists, it takes priority over default work block extraction.

pages.title: Input Port
pages.text: Input ports only receive items. The network tries ordinary targets first, then filtered input ports.

pages.title: Filtering by Processing Step
pages.text: Ports have filter slots plus a whitelist/blacklist toggle. Put a $(l)processed tea leaf$() in a filter slot and the pipe matches by $(l)processing subset$(): a passing leaf is accepted when it $(l)contains all$() steps recorded on the sample.$(br2)Example: a sample with Fixing lets [Fixing], [Fixing+Rolling] and [Fixing+Rolling+Drying] through, while [Withering] and fresh leaves do not pass.$(br2)A sample of $(l)fresh leaf$() only matches other fresh leaves.$(br2)All other items still match the old way: item and NBT must be identical.

pages.title: Filter Troubleshooting
pages.text: If a filter slot will not accept a sample or the result looks wrong, check: $(li)whitelist allows matching items, blacklist blocks them;$(li)the sample itself must carry processing steps — a fresh leaf only matches fresh leaves;$(li)if the network has no valid target, items stay where they are.
